page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor on the x86_64 architecture. The system features 32 physical cores with a single thread per core and a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, operating under a shared CPU allocation model via KVM virtualization. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, the server bundles three NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a total of 144 GB of VRAM. No local storage is included in this configuration, though it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng, as well as PassMark CPU and physics tests. The AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 vector and neural network instructions and cryptography extensions like VAES and SHA_NI. Memory performance is strong, with uncached read bandwidth reaching 331.99 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 123.17 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET throughput also rank in the top tier, with Redis handling 128.07 million operations per second. However, Geekbench ray tracing performance is average, falling in the middle tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers high resource density by combining substantial system memory with triple enterprise-grade GPUs, making it a viable option for heavy parallel processing without the overhead of dedicated physical infrastructure. A notable tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage solutions for persistent data. This server is suited for GPU-accelerated workloads, machine learning model training, large-scale data processing, image processing, and high-throughput database operations.
